svg.text: Randomised timeouts, one vote per term, majority wins - and why a split vote is harmless

g.text: every node starts as a FOLLOWER
every node starts as a FOLLOWER
one vote per peer per term
one vote per peer per term
a split vote just ends the term
a split vote just ends the term
why a range, not a value
the timeout is RANDOMISED per node:
so the three nodes rarely time out
together, and a split vote is rare
AND no vote cast this term
AND candidate log is not behind
A node that hears nothing from a leader for its election timeout assumes there is none.
arcadedb.ha.electionTimeoutMin=5000 / electionTimeoutMax=10000 (ms) - Ratis picks a random value in that range per node
The first node to time out increments the term, becomes a CANDIDATE and votes for itself.
term 0 -> term 1; votes for itself = 1 of 3; a majority of 3 is 2
The candidate asks the other nodes for their vote, over the Raft port, not over HTTP.
RequestVote(term, candidateId, lastLogIndex, lastLogTerm) - Ratis gRPC on arcadedb.ha.raft.port = 2434
A peer grants its single vote only if the candidate's log is at least as up to date as its own.
a candidate whose lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm is behind is refused, which is what keeps committed entries safe
Two of three is a majority, so the candidate becomes leader for term 1 - and only for term 1.
exactly one leader can exist per term: two majorities of the same cluster always share at least one node
The leader sends empty AppendEntries on a timer; every one of them resets the followers' election timers.
the heartbeat interval is well under electionTimeoutMin, so a healthy leader is never voted out
If two candidates start at once nobody reaches a majority; the term ends with no leader and the timers re-randomise.
no leader is ever elected by a minority, so a split vote costs one election round, never correctness
Election state is observable and steerable from outside the cluster, which is what the HA tests drive.
